pep723.description: PEP 723 inline script metadata in tools/*.py. Renovate's pep723 manager ships an EMPTY managerFilePatterns and is therefore opt-in: without this block it extracts nothing, and the wordfreq packageRule below would match a dep that was never produced — reading as coverage while providing none.

lockFileMaintenance.description: flake.lock. Both inputs (nixpkgs, flake-parts) are branch refs, so lockFileMaintenance is the only thing that moves them; there is nothing else in this repo with a lockfile.

customManagers.description: Tool pins in .github/workflows/*.yml. ruff and pyright are invoked through `uvx <tool>@<version>` so that CI is reproducible rather than 'whatever shipped this morning' — which means nothing else would ever tell us they had gone stale. The marker comment sits directly above the env var it names, and EVERY workflow that pins CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION carries one: three of them do, a bump must move all three together, and a pin without the marker is one this manager cannot see — live.yml had exactly that and silently forked off check.yml's build. test_every_workflow_pins_the_same_claude_code_build is the assertion that keeps them equal.

packageRules.description: wordfreq is dashboard-gated because a bump is a RETRIEVAL CHANGE, not a dependency update. It is not a runtime dependency at all — no adopter ever resolves it — it is the resolver behind the committed src/memkit/common-words.txt, and that file decides which query terms the recall hook floors as conversational coincidence. Bumping the pin therefore changes what every consumer's every-prompt hook injects, via a PR whose diff is a wordlist. A green CI proves only that the artifact matches the new pin (the `wordlist` job regenerates and diffs), which is precisely the wrong thing to automerge on. A human takes this one, regenerates the artifact in the same PR, and reads the word-set diff. Both managers are named because the pin is duplicated by construction: pyproject's extra is what a maintainer installs, the PEP 723 block is what `uv run` resolves, and tools/check-wordlist-reproducible.py is red if they disagree — so they must move together, hence the shared groupName.

Claude Code is dashboard-gated for the same reason wordfreq is: a bump is not a dependency update but a change to the HARNESS whose measured behaviour this plugin is built on. The option-name mangling that carries the config, the trailing slash on the plugin root, and the fact that exit 2 on UserPromptSubmit blocks the turn rather than merely failing — the zero-argument pin exists because of that last one — were each measured against a specific build. What CI re-measures on a bump: the rig's CLI tier covers validation, install and what the harness recorded in its settings, and the HARNESS tier takes a real turn with the model routed somewhere unreachable, which is what puts option delivery, config resolution and injection under a required check — hook dispatch precedes the model call, so none of that needs credentials. What still needs a model, and so is invisible to a green PR: a hook's stdout reaching the turn, and double-registration detection across several turns. So a human takes this one, runs `MEMKIT_RIG_LIVE=1 pytest tests/rig` on the new build, and says so in the PR.

3-day cooldown on GitHub Actions bumps. Actions are the highest-value target in this repo — they are the only third-party code that runs with a write-capable token — and the tj-actions/changed-files class of compromise (Mar 2025) was caught publicly inside a day, so a short wait covers it. Deliberately NOT widened to flake inputs: the nix manager's datasource is git-refs, which carries no timestamps, and under `minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour: timestamp-required` a missing timestamp HOLDS the update — a repo-wide cooldown would silently freeze every flake input rather than error.
